original_question: Zavorotnyi proved that the fourth moment I2(T) of the Riemann zeta function has the asymptotic I2(T) = T P4(log T) + O(T^(2/3 + epsilon)), where P4 is a specific polynomial of degree 4. Improve the exponent in this error term.
target_in_paper: Section "Problems" → "Moments of the Riemann zeta function," Problem (3). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it identifies the same problem about the classical fourth moment I_2(T) of the Riemann zeta function, quotes Zavorotnyi’s 1989 asymptotic with a specific degree-4 polynomial P_4, and asks for exactly what the paper asks for—an improvement of the error term, not a different theorem. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should define I_2(T) explicitly as I_2(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^4 dt, using the paper’s notation I_k(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^(2k) dt. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

It should state the asymptotic regime T→∞ and make the ε-quantifier explicit. By standard analytic-number-theory convention, the paper’s O(T^(2/3+ε)) is read as: for every ε>0, one seeks a bound of that shape as T→∞. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

It should say that P_4 is the same specific degree-4 polynomial already appearing in Zavorotnyi’s asymptotic; the problem is not asking for a new polynomial or a reformulation of the main term. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

It should clarify the scope: the paper asks only for any improvement over the exponent 2/3 in the fourth-moment error term, not for the broader general conjecture for E_k(T) and not even explicitly for the conjecturally optimal exponent 1/2 discussed separately in Problem (4). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
refined_question: Let I_2(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^4 dt, where ζ(s) is the Riemann zeta function. Zavorotnyi proved in 1989 that, as T→∞, I_2(T)=T P_4(log T)+O(T^(2/3+ε)) for every ε>0, where P_4 is the specific degree-4 polynomial occurring in this fourth-moment asymptotic. Prove a stronger error term by showing that there exists θ<2/3 such that I_2(T)=T P_4(log T)+O(T^(θ+ε)) for every ε>0. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if E_2(T):=I_2(T)-T P_4(log T), improve Zavorotnyi’s bound by proving E_2(T)=O(T^(θ+ε)) for every ε>0 and some θ<2/3. This is the k=2 specialization of the paper’s nearby definition E_k(T)=I_k(T)-T P_{k^2}(log T). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem (3) in the paper’s subsection "Moments of the Riemann zeta function": it states Zavorotnyi’s asymptotic I_2(T)=T P_4(log T)+O(T^(2/3+ε)), says that P_4 is a specific degree-4 polynomial, and asks to “Improve the bound in the error term.” The notation section supplies the definition of I_2(T), and nearby Problem (4) shows that broader questions about the general error term E_k(T) and conjectural optimal exponents are separate problems. So the paper-faithful rewrite should stay narrowly focused on improving the known fourth-moment exponent 2/3. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
